transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. It's nice to meet you too. 

Well, I'm here because I just... I can't stop seeing this droop and unevenness around my mouth and jaw. It's all I see in every photo and every time I look in a reflection. People keep telling me I look fine, but it feels so incredibly obvious to me. It's gotten to the point where I've actually started avoiding giving presentations at work, and I'm even getting out of meeting with my clients because I don't want them looking at it.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking your mouth or jaw in mirrors, photos, or other reflections?

Yes, all the time. Before I leave for work, or if we have a family event, I can spend hours just checking myself in the bathroom mirror. I take pictures on my phone from different angles to see exactly how bad it looks. Then I'll end up redoing my makeup over and over, or I'll try to arrange a scarf to hide my jawline. 

I also constantly ask my husband if my face looks lopsided to him. And... I usually end up scrolling through pictures of other women on my phone, just comparing my face to theirs to see how much worse mine looks beside them. It really takes up a lot of my time.
Has a doctor or anyone else ever told you there is actually something noticeably wrong with your mouth or jaw?

No, no one has. Actually, it's... it's the exact opposite. Like I mentioned, my husband and everyone else just tell me I look fine, or they say they don't see what I'm talking about at all. I've never had a doctor or a dentist point it out either. But... I mean, I know what I'm seeing in the mirror, even if no one else admits to seeing it.
Do you believe your mouth and jaw actually look abnormal to other people?

Well, I'm not really sure what other people see, honestly. I mean... I know what I see, and to me, it's glaringly obvious. But since everyone keeps telling me they don't notice it, I don't know if they're just being polite or if they genuinely don't see how bad it is. I just feel like they must be able to see it, even if they won't say it.
Are you certain that your mouth and jaw are truly abnormal, despite what other people say?

I'm... I'm not completely certain, no. I mean, I see it clearly. To me, it's very real and it looks awful. But when my husband and everyone else swear they don't see anything wrong, it does make me question things a little bit. 

I just... I don't really have a solid answer for you. I just know what I see when I look in the mirror, even if I can't be one hundred percent sure of what's actually real anymore.
When you have to speak in front of other people, do you get a sudden rush of intense fear?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I get very self-conscious, and I hate when people look at me while I'm talking because I worry they're staring at my mouth... but I don't get a sudden rush of intense fear. It's not like a panic that just hits me. I just feel really uncomfortable.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day nearly every day?

No, I don't think so. I mean... I definitely get frustrated, and it's exhausting dealing with my appearance. But I wouldn't say I feel depressed or down all day, every day. It's really just... my distress is mostly tied to worrying about my face, rather than just feeling sad all the time.
Are these checking and comparing behaviors mainly because of your worry about how your mouth and jaw look?

Yes, absolutely. It's all because of that. 

Before I go to work, or even just before a family event, I can spend hours checking the bathroom mirror. I take pictures on my phone from all different angles to see how it looks. I'll redo my makeup, adjust my scarf over and over to try and hide it... I constantly ask my husband if my face looks lopsided today. And then I end up scrolling through photos of other women, just to see how bad my mouth and jaw look compared to theirs. 

So yes, all of that checking and comparing is entirely driven by how much I worry about my face.
Outside of worrying about your mouth and jaw, do you also spend a lot of time worrying about many other things in your life?

No, not really. I mean, I have normal everyday things, like stress from work... but I don't spend a lot of time worrying about other areas of my life. It really is just my face. Almost all of my anxiety and worry goes straight to how my mouth and jaw look. If it weren't for that, I don't think I'd be a very worried person at all.
Do you feel driven to check or compare your face because you have to do it to ease anxiety, even when you know it doesn’t really make sense?

I don't really know if I'd say it doesn't make sense to me. I mean, I check because I need to know how bad it looks, and yes, it does relieve the anxiety for a minute if I think I've managed to hide it well enough. But it's not like I'm doing it for no reason. I do it because my face is actually lopsided. I have to check.
Aside from your concerns about how your mouth and jaw look, do you have any other unwanted thoughts that keep coming into your mind over and over?

No, I don't think so. I mean, my mind is pretty much consumed by my mouth and jaw, so... there really isn't room for much else. But no, I don't have any other unwanted thoughts that just keep popping into my head like that. It really is just about my face.
Have you ever had to do repetitive rituals about anything other than your appearance?

No, I haven't. I don't do anything like that... you know, like checking the stove or washing my hands over and over, if that's what you mean. All of my routines are just about my face. Everything I do repeatedly is just to check my jaw or try to fix how my mouth looks. There's nothing else.
